subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observe/mirror mode, and if so should it be read-only session observation, bidirectional native-channel mirroring, or limited to same-session live updates?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the remaining behavior changes cross-channel disclosure, message retention, public CLI/config surface, and session-state semantics, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Guarded read-only observe mode
options.body: Add a default-off TUI observer that can display approved agent/channel activity without sending messages back to native channels, with explicit redaction, auth, and docs.

options.title: Only fix same-session live updates
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/38829 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96252 as the current repair path and leave broader cross-channel observation out of scope for now.

options.title: Bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and native channels to mirror messages both ways, accepting a larger channel-routing and security design before implementation.

recommendation.title: Guarded read-only observe mode
recommendation.body: Add a default-off TUI observer that can display approved agent/channel activity without sending messages back to native channels, with explicit redaction, auth, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current signal on the related TUI live-session PR and this needs product/security direction across TUI, Gateway, and channel surfaces.
